j-future.name: Future forms (GB9)
j-future.tip: Decision now → will. Plan made before → be going to. Fixed arrangement → am/is/are + -ing. After will → base verb only.
j-future.uz: Hozir qaror qilsangiz — will. Oldindan reja — going to. Aniq kelishuv — am/is/are + -ing.

j-compare.name: Comparatives & superlatives (GB10)
j-compare.tip: Two things → -er / more … than. Three or more → the -est / the most. good → better → the best, bad → worse → the worst.
j-compare.uz: Ikki narsa — -er / more … than. Eng … — the -est / the most.

j-pp.name: Present Perfect: ever/never, for/since (GB11)
j-pp.tip: have/has + V3. for + a length of time (for 3 years). since + a starting point (since 2020, since Monday).
j-pp.uz: for — qancha vaqt; since — qachondan beri. Ingliz tilida bu Present Perfect bilan aytiladi.

j-ppps.name: Present Perfect vs Past Simple (GB12)
j-ppps.tip: Finished time (yesterday, ago, last week, in 2020) → Past Simple. No time, or ever/never/since/for → Present Perfect.
j-ppps.uz: Tugagan vaqt aytilsa — Past Simple. Vaqt aytilmasa yoki since/for bo'lsa — Present Perfect.

j-modals.name: Modals (GB13)
j-modals.tip: Past ability → could. Forbidden → mustn't. Not necessary → don't have to. Advice → should. After a modal → base verb, no 'to' (except have to).
j-modals.uz: mustn't — taqiqlangan; don't have to — shart emas. Modaldan keyin fe'l oddiy shaklda.

j-pastcont.name: Past Continuous with when/while (GB14)
j-pastcont.tip: Long action → was/were + -ing. Short action that interrupts it → Past Simple. when + short action, while + long action.
j-pastcont.uz: Uzun ish — was/were + -ing. Uni bo'lgan qisqa ish — Past Simple.

j-vocab.name: Vocabulary (B1 articles)
j-vocab.tip: Revise the word lists from The Benefits of Volunteering, The Rise of Online Shopping and Working from Home.

j-reading.name: Reading: True / False
j-reading.tip: Find the part of the text that matches the sentence. If the text says the opposite, the answer is False.
j-reading.uz: Gapga mos joyni matndan toping. Matn teskarisini aytsa — False.

s-passive.name: Passive voice (SGB5)
s-passive.tip: be + past participle. Choose the tense of 'be': is done, is being done, was done, will be done, has been done. Use 'by' only when the doer matters.

s-data.name: Data language (SGB6)
s-data.tip: fewer + countable nouns, less + uncountable nouns. twice as much/many as. rise/rose/risen, fall/fell/fallen. from X to Y; by = the size of the change.

s-spec.name: Speculation (SGB8)
s-spec.tip: Present: must / might / can't + base verb. Past: must / might / can't + have + past participle.

s-verbpat.name: Verb patterns (SGB9)
s-verbpat.tip: verb + -ing: avoid, consider, suggest, look forward to. verb + object + to-infinitive: encourage, advise, allow.

s-wordform.name: Word formation
s-wordform.tip: Suffixes change the word class (aware → awareness). Prefixes change the meaning: mis- = wrongly, un-/im-/il- = not, re- = again.

s-vocab.name: Vocabulary (C1 articles)
s-vocab.tip: Revise the word lists from Urban Green Space, The Economics of Attention and Automation and the Future of Work.

s-reading.name: Reading: True / False / Not Given
s-reading.tip: FALSE = the text says the opposite. NOT GIVEN = the text does not say anything about it. Don't use your own knowledge.

jp1.title: Working from Home
jp1.text: Since 2020, many companies have let their employees work from home. Most workers enjoy the flexibility: they can start work earlier or later, and they do not have to commute. This saves both time and money. However, working from home is not perfect. Some people feel isolated because they do not see their colleagues every day. Others find it hard to stop working in the evening. Many companies now choose a compromise: employees work at home for two or three days a week and come to the office on the other days.

sp1.title: Automation and Work
sp1.text: Automation is changing the labour market faster than many governments expected. In some factories, robots now do tasks that once required dozens of workers, and many of those workers have been made redundant. However, automation also creates new jobs, especially in maintenance and software. The problem is that these jobs require skills that the old workers often do not have. For this reason, several countries have introduced reskilling programmes. Critics argue that these programmes are too short to be effective, but supporters say they are the only realistic option.

questions.prompt: — The phone is ringing. — I ___ it!
questions.explain: You decide at the moment of speaking → will ('ll).

questions.prompt: My brother ___ engineering next year. He decided last month.
questions.explain: A plan made before now → be going to.

questions.prompt: We ___ our cousins at 7 o'clock tonight. The table is booked.
questions.explain: A fixed arrangement with a time and place → Present Continuous.

questions.prompt: I think it ___ tomorrow. (rain)
questions.explain: An opinion about the future (I think …) → will + base verb.

questions.prompt: He will studying next year.
options: He will to study next year.
questions.explain: After will → base verb only: no -ing, no 'to', no -s.

questions.prompt: This is ___ traffic jam I have ever seen.
questions.explain: bad → worse → the worst. 'the … I have ever seen' → superlative.

questions.prompt: Online shopping is ___ than going to a shop. (convenient)
questions.explain: Long adjective + than → more + adjective.

questions.prompt: Tashkent is ___ Namangan.
questions.explain: Short adjective: big → bigger (double g) + than.

questions.prompt: January is ___ month of the year. (cold)
questions.explain: One of a group of many → the + -est.

questions.prompt: She is more tall than me.
options: She is more taller than me.
She is the tallest than me.
questions.explain: Short adjective → -er. Never use 'more' and '-er' together.

questions.prompt: She has lived here ___ 2019.
questions.explain: 2019 is a starting point → since.

questions.prompt: We have known each other ___ five years.
questions.explain: Five years is a length of time → for.

questions.prompt: ___ you ever ___ for a charity?
questions.explain: Life experience with 'ever' → Have + subject + V3.

questions.prompt: I have never ___ sushi. (eat)
questions.explain: have + V3: eat → ate → eaten.

questions.prompt: I live here since 2020.
questions.explain: It started in the past and is still true → Present Perfect with since. Don't translate word for word from Uzbek.

questions.prompt: I ___ Aziz yesterday.
questions.explain: 'yesterday' is a finished time → Past Simple.

questions.prompt: We ___ our manager since Monday.
questions.explain: since → Present Perfect.

questions.prompt: I ___ to Istanbul two years ago.
questions.explain: 'ago' means a finished time → Past Simple.

questions.prompt: My father ___ for this company since 2010. (work)
questions.explain: since + it is still true → has + V3.

questions.prompt: Have you watched the match last night?
options: Did you watch the match last night?
Have you watch the match last night?
Did you watched the match last night?
Were you watch the match last night?
questions.answer: Did you watch the match last night?
questions.explain: 'last night' is a finished time → Past Simple: Did + subject + base verb.

questions.prompt: When I was young, I ___ swim very well.
questions.explain: Ability in the past → could.

questions.prompt: It's a holiday tomorrow. We ___ go to school.
questions.explain: Not necessary → don't have to.

questions.prompt: You ___ use your phone in the exam. It's not allowed.
questions.explain: Forbidden → mustn't.

questions.prompt: You look really tired. You ___ go to bed earlier.
questions.explain: Advice → should.

questions.prompt: He can to play the guitar.
questions.explain: After can → base verb: no 'to', no -s, no -ing.

questions.prompt: When the manager called at 10 a.m., we ___ a video meeting.
questions.explain: A long action in progress, interrupted by a call → was/were + -ing.

questions.prompt: I was cooking when the phone ___. (ring)
questions.explain: A short action that interrupts → Past Simple: ring → rang.

questions.prompt: ___ I was walking home, it started to rain.
questions.explain: while + a long action (was walking).

questions.prompt: They ___ football at 5 o'clock yesterday. (play)
questions.explain: An action in progress at a time in the past → were + -ing.

questions.prompt: When the lights went out, we watching a film.
options: When the lights went out, we were watching a film.
When the lights went out, we was watching a film.
When the lights went out, we watch a film.
When the lights were going out, we watching a film.
questions.answer: When the lights went out, we were watching a film.
questions.explain: Don't forget was/were: we were watching.

questions.prompt: Commuting means ___.
options: travelling regularly between home and work or school
questions.answer: travelling regularly between home and work or school
questions.explain: commute = to travel to work or school and back every day.

questions.prompt: If you feel isolated, you feel ___.
options: alone and without contact with other people
questions.answer: alone and without contact with other people
questions.explain: isolated = alone, cut off from other people.

questions.prompt: If the benefits outweigh the problems, the benefits are ___.
questions.explain: outweigh = to be bigger or more important than something.

questions.prompt: Small shops find it hard to ___ with huge online companies.
questions.explain: compete with = to try to be more successful than someone.

questions.prompt: Volunteering gives many retired people a sense of ___ — they feel useful again.
questions.explain: a sense of purpose = a feeling that your life has a reason.

questions.prompt: Many small shops are in ___ because more people now buy online.
questions.explain: in decline = becoming smaller or weaker.

questions.prompt: Delivery vans produce large amounts of ___, which pollute the air.
questions.explain: emissions = gases that go into the air, e.g. from cars.

questions.prompt: "Overall" means ___.
options: in general, when you consider everything
questions.answer: in general, when you consider everything
questions.explain: overall = in general, when you think about everything together.

questions.prompt: People who work from home do not have to travel to the office.
questions.explain: "they do not have to commute".

questions.prompt: Everyone feels happier when they work from home.
questions.explain: "Some people feel isolated", so not everyone is happier.

questions.prompt: Working from home can save money.
questions.explain: "This saves both time and money."

questions.prompt: Many companies now ask employees to come to the office every day.
questions.explain: They work at home for two or three days a week.

questions.prompt: The results of the national survey ___ next week.
questions.explain: Results don't publish themselves → future passive: will be + past participle.

questions.prompt: The new software is testing this week.
options: The new software is being tested this week.
The new software is tested by this week.
The new software is been tested this week.
The new software has testing this week.
questions.answer: The new software is being tested this week.
questions.explain: An action in progress now, in the passive → is being + past participle.

questions.prompt: The bridge ___ in 1998.
questions.explain: Finished past time, passive → was/were + past participle.

questions.prompt: Millions of parcels ___ every day. (deliver)
questions.explain: A general fact in the passive, plural subject → are + past participle.

questions.prompt: A new law ___ by parliament at the moment.
questions.explain: 'at the moment' → present continuous passive: is being + past participle.

questions.prompt: There were ___ cars on the roads in 2020 than in 2019.
questions.explain: cars are countable → fewer.

questions.prompt: Doctors earn two times more than nurses.
options: Doctors earn twice as much as nurses.
Doctors earn twice more as nurses.
Doctors earn two times as many as nurses.
Doctors earn twice as much than nurses.
questions.answer: Doctors earn twice as much as nurses.
questions.explain: twice as much (uncountable: money) as.

questions.prompt: The number of visitors ___ from 2,000 to 5,000 between 2015 and 2025.
questions.explain: rise → rose → risen. It has no object and no passive. 'Raise' needs an object.

questions.prompt: Unemployment fell ___ 8% ___ 5%.
questions.explain: from (the start) to (the end). 'by' gives the size of the change (by 3%).

questions.prompt: Average screen time has doubled. It is now ___ it was in 2015.
questions.explain: twice as + adjective + as.

questions.prompt: That ___ be Aziz on the phone — he's on a plane to London right now.
questions.explain: We are sure it is impossible → can't.

questions.prompt: She has a high temperature and a bad cough. She ___ be ill.
questions.explain: We are almost sure, based on evidence → must.

questions.prompt: The streets are wet. It ___ rained last night.
questions.explain: A conclusion about the past → must have + past participle.

questions.prompt: He hasn't replied. He ___ seen my email — maybe it went to spam.
questions.explain: A possibility about the past → might (not) have + past participle.

questions.prompt: She must has forgotten the meeting.
options: She must have forgotten the meeting.
She must had forgotten the meeting.
She must to have forgotten the meeting.
questions.answer: She must have forgotten the meeting.
questions.explain: modal + have (never has/had) + past participle.

questions.prompt: My parents encouraged me ___ for the scholarship.
questions.explain: encourage + object + to-infinitive.

questions.prompt: I look forward to meet you at the conference.
options: I look forward to meeting you at the conference.
I look forward meeting you at the conference.
I look forward to met you at the conference.
I look forward for meeting you at the conference.
questions.answer: I look forward to meeting you at the conference.
questions.explain: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition → verb + -ing.

questions.prompt: Students should avoid ___ their phones while studying.
questions.explain: avoid + -ing.

questions.prompt: The teacher advised us ___ our notes before the exam.
questions.explain: advise + object + to-infinitive.

questions.prompt: Have you considered ___ abroad?
questions.explain: consider + -ing.

questions.prompt: Public ___ of the health risks of sitting all day has grown. (aware)
questions.explain: We need a noun here: aware + -ness → awareness.

questions.prompt: Some websites deliberately ___ their readers. (inform — use a prefix meaning 'wrongly')
questions.explain: mis- = wrongly → misinform (one s).

questions.prompt: It is ___ to read a 300-page report in one hour.
questions.explain: Before p, b and m, the prefix in- becomes im-.

questions.prompt: Many factory workers are now ___ because robots do their jobs. (employ)
questions.explain: un- (not) + employ + -ed → unemployed.

questions.prompt: The government launched a ___ programme to help factory workers learn new skills. (skill — use a prefix meaning 'again' and -ing)
questions.explain: re- (again) + skill + -ing → reskilling.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'not legal'?
questions.explain: Before l, the prefix in- becomes il-.

questions.prompt: Biodiversity means ___.
options: the variety of plant and animal life in an area
the number of people who live in a city
the speed at which cities grow
questions.answer: the variety of plant and animal life in an area
questions.explain: bio (life) + diversity (variety).

questions.prompt: If a worker is made redundant, ___.
options: they are promoted to a higher position
they choose to work fewer hours
they lose their job because it is no longer needed
questions.answer: they lose their job because it is no longer needed
questions.explain: redundant = no longer needed.

questions.prompt: A compulsive habit is one that ___.
options: is very hard to stop or control
other people force you to do
questions.answer: is very hard to stop or control
questions.explain: compulsive = impossible to control.

questions.prompt: If something is done inadvertently, it is done ___.
questions.explain: inadvertently = by accident, not on purpose.

questions.prompt: The new ramp makes the library ___ to wheelchair users.
questions.explain: accessible = easy to reach, enter or use.

questions.prompt: Constant notifications lead to the ___ of our attention into tiny pieces.
questions.explain: fragmentation = breaking into small pieces.

questions.prompt: Moving to a new country is one of the biggest ___ a family can experience.
questions.explain: upheaval = a big, sudden change that causes disruption.

questions.prompt: Housing in the city centre has become ___ expensive for most young families.
questions.explain: prohibitively expensive = so expensive that people cannot buy it.

questions.prompt: Several studies have found that regular physical activity ___ with better sleep.
questions.explain: correlate with = to have a connection with, so the two change together.

questions.prompt: Planting more trees can help ___ the effects of extreme heat in cities.
questions.explain: mitigate = to make something bad less serious.

questions.prompt: Automation has changed the labour market more slowly than governments expected.
questions.explain: The text says "faster than many governments expected".

questions.prompt: Automation creates new jobs in software.
questions.explain: "automation also creates new jobs, especially in maintenance and software".

questions.prompt: Reskilling programmes are free for all workers.
questions.explain: The text does not say anything about the cost of the programmes.

questions.prompt: Everyone agrees that reskilling programmes are effective.
questions.explain: "Critics argue that these programmes are too short to be effective".
